customManagers.description: Version pins no built-in manager reads, under pkgs/ and hosts/: from-source and release-binary packages, container tags, PyPI overrides. Opt-in per pin via a `# renovate:` comment directly above a `version`-like binding (`version`, `brainVersion`…), so the ones left out stay out; each excluded pin says why in its own file.
Commit pins on untagged upstreams: Renovate follows the branch head (git-refs) and rewrites `rev`. No versioningTemplate: git-refs needs its default `git` versioning.
The Renovate version the self-hosted workflow runs (.github/workflows/renovate.yml), so Renovate keeps itself current.

NixOS release channel: nixpkgs, nix-darwin and home-manager follow the YY.MM release branches in flake.nix. Renovate watches nixpkgs' plain YY.MM tags (cut on release day; -pre/-beta excluded) and rewrites all three refs in one PR.

lockFileMaintenance.description: All day Monday, not the default 'before 4am': GitHub drops most of the 2-hourly scheduled runs, and none landed in 00:00–04:00 UTC on a Monday from 2026-09-28 to 2026-10-19, so no lock-file PR was opened for four weeks.

packageRules.description: Minor and patch bumps of pkgs/, hosts/ and GitHub Actions merge themselves once CI is green: CI builds the rpi5 system, which is the check that matters for a version-and-hash bump (a reviewer only sees the hash). Three days of minimumReleaseAge give upstream time to pull a broken release. Pins nBookPro builds are excluded by the next rule. The nix manager (flake inputs, flake.lock) is left out: one lock refresh moves nixpkgs for the whole system and a green build does not prove the services run, so those stay with Nico. Rules further down override it: nixos-release never merges itself, claude-code and t3code wait 1 day. What merged shows in Hermes's 09:00 digest next to the units failing on rpi5 (hosts/rpi5/agents/hermes/workspace/daily-pending-digest.sh).
Majors wait for Nico, grouped in one PR opened on Mondays: one approval a week instead of one per dependency.

Pins nBookPro builds stay manual: pre-merge CI evaluates nBookPro but builds only rpi5, so a darwin archive that changed shape (entire's git-remote-entire, say) would merge green and fail only in deploy-nbookpro after main moved. claude-code and t3code keep their own automerge (their rules come later). A new pin the Mac builds belongs in this list.

hermes-agent is pinned to a release tag in flake.nix and follows nixpkgs-unstable. Only plain vX.Y.Z tags: upstream also cuts daily `vX.Y.Z+canary.<date>` snapshots of main, and its old date tags (v2026.9.24) sort above v0.x as semver. A bump whose nix/lib.nix names a nodejs_* our nixpkgs-unstable lacks fails `eval rpi5` on the PR. A green PR can still drop something the config names, so read the release notes before approving.
prBodyNotes: Read the release notes before approving. Checks catch eval and build breaks, not a bundled plugin that moved: v0.22 moved the `holographic` memory provider (`memory.provider` in hosts/rpi5/agents/hermes/hermes.nix) to the plugin catalog, and Hermes would have started without its fact store.

packageRules.description: claude-code follows the `next` dist-tag, not `latest`. The two diverge by days and the gap is load-bearing: Anthropic gates models on the client version, so `latest` (2.1.278 when this was written) answers --model claude-opus-5-5 with a 400 telling you to upgrade, while `next` (2.1.280) serves it and resolves the bare `opus` alias to it. Following `latest` would mean the newest model is unreachable for as long as the tags disagree. The cost is riding a pre-release channel on purpose — read the release notes on the PR. Merges itself once CI is green: the Renovate App bypasses the review (.github/settings.yml) and Renovate merges through the API (platformAutomerge off), so no human gate and no armed auto-merge in between. minimumReleaseAge is 1 day, no longer: `next` moves about daily and followTag leaves only the tag's version as a candidate, so an age above the gap between releases (3 days: never met, 2026-11-14) means it never merges.

t3code follows stable releases (upstream's Beta channel stopped at 0.1.10). The rpi5 server and the Mac app ship together from one version: a server and app on different versions lose sessions over T3 Connect. Merges itself once CI is green, which includes t3code-fork-release.yml building the fork release and pinning its hashes on the PR (Renovate waits for every check, required or not); the Renovate App bypasses the review (.github/settings.yml). minimumReleaseAge lets a broken nightly be pulled before it reaches the Pi and the Mac. No concurrency limit: from 2026-11-15 to 11-21 the bump sat Rate-Limited behind 10 open renovate/* branches.
Keep each agent CLI's Nix flake source tag and mirrored package version in one update PR.
Keep each agent CLI's Nix flake source tag and mirrored package version in one update PR.

pkgs/ and hosts/ bumps: Renovate rewrites `version` via the regex manager, and postUpgradeTasks recomputes the fixed-output hashes beside it (scripts/nix-fix-hashes.py) before committing, so the bump and its hashes land as one commit. Needs the self-hosted runner (.github/workflows/renovate.yml) — the Mend app ignores postUpgradeTasks. Dependency-store hashes (pnpmDeps, vendorHash, cargoHash) are recomputed by building that one fixed-output derivation; the `hashes` check stays as the gate for anything the script still cannot speak for. The `src` half only holds because every fetcher under pkgs/ passes an explicit version-bearing `name` — see pkgs/README.md, 'Fixed-output names'.
prBodyNotes: Pinned hashes (`hash`, per-platform hashes, `imageDigest`, `npmDepsHash`, `pnpmDeps.hash`, `vendorHash`, `cargoHash`) were recomputed in this same commit by `scripts/nix-fix-hashes.py` (postUpgradeTasks, self-hosted Renovate in .github/workflows/renovate.yml).
A package the script cannot `callPackage` with `{ }` (e.g. one fed by a flake input) is reported, not fixed — check the `hashes` log, and fix it with `lib.fakeHash` + a real build.
Check the upstream changelog before merging — a major bump may also need module changes. `affine-mcp-server` 1.x → 3.x, for instance, reworks authentication.

packageRules.description: npm is read only for open-knowledge's lockfile. Its own version is tracked by the regex manager on default.nix, and scripts/t3code-fork is not a Nix package, so no npm version bump is proposed.

Transitive fixes (hono, zod, simple-git…) land by refreshing open-knowledge's lockfile: Renovate cannot target a transitive dependency on its own, and Dependabot's PRs for them edited package-lock.json without re-pinning npmDepsHash, so build rpi5 failed and nobody merged them. In its own branch apart from flake.lock, merged once CI is green; default.nix reads the lock through importNpmLock, so no hash to re-pin, and the pkgs/** hash task is switched off for it (it would target package.json). Exempt from the concurrent-branch cap (10): stale PRs fill it.

NixOS release bump (26.05 → 26.11…): one PR rewriting the nixpkgs, nix-darwin and home-manager refs together, opened 3 days after nixpkgs tags the release so the nix-darwin and home-manager branches exist. Never merges itself: a release bump needs a human read of the release notes (Renovate gets no review, .github/settings.yml). The regex manager has no lock step, so flake.lock still names the old branches; CI re-locks in memory, so its checks test the new release.
prBodyNotes: Before merging: run `nix flake update nixpkgs darwin home-manager` on this branch and push it, so flake.lock follows the new branches (Renovate's regex manager does not touch the lock).

Read the NixOS release notes (https://nixos.org/manual/nixos/stable/release-notes) and drop the `# no-renovate: temporary` overrides and overlays the release makes redundant (AGENTS.md, Pinned dependencies). Keep `system.stateVersion` as it is.
The rpi5 deploy unpacks the whole new closure: check free space on the Pi first (see the min-free note in hosts/rpi5/configuration.nix).

vulnerabilityAlerts.description: Fixes for a vulnerable direct dependency merge themselves once CI is green (the App bypasses the review, .github/settings.yml).
